newsitem.title: UK: NZ's Birch sees price stability for next three yrs.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch sees price stability for next three yrs.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch on Monday painted a rosy economic outlook for New Zealand and said price stability was excellent.
"Price stability is excellent with inflation expected to remain under two percent over the next three years," Birch told journalists here.
Birch, in London to shore up investor confidence in New Zealand's new coalition government, said the recent rise in the New Zealand dollar may have a small lagged effect on the country's exports.
"There may be a little lag in respect of the effect of the currency (on exports)," Birch said.

He said he was delighted with the contribution that exports had made to New Zealand growth in the December quarter last year. Production-based GDP rose 0.7 percent in the December quarter for an actual annual change of 2.7 percent.
Birch said he had seen no investor nervousness towards the coalition government during his trip to London.
"People have been extraordinarily well informed," he said.
Asked if he was concerned about New Zealand's current account deficit, Birch said "No, a current account deficit has been a feature of our economy for several years."
New Zealand's Reserve Bank has warned that the forecast current account deficit of 5.5 percent on average over the next three years is unsustainable.

Birch said he expected economic growth to rise to three percent in 1997/98 and four percent the following year. He said he forecast a government surplus of 2.5 to 3.0 percent allowing the debt to GDP ratio to get to 20 percent within three years. He declined to comment on whether interest rates should be lower.
"That's a matter for the Reserve Bank," he said.
